factors.title: Herding-aware poll weighting
factors.detail: When a Senate poll average sits far from fundamentals, its weight shrinks: x max(0.5, 1 - 0.04 x (gap - 1 pt)), and race uncertainty widens 0.1 pt per gap point. Party-neutral.

factors.title: Demographic + regional error
factors.detail: A shared Hispanic-voter polling miss (sd 6 pts, scaled by each state's 2020 Census Hispanic share) plus a Census-region error (sd 1.5) on top of national, state and race error.

factors.title: Expert ratings in the House
factors.detail: Cook/Sabato/Inside-style ratings converted to margins (Toss-up 0, Tilt 2, Lean 4.5, Likely 9, Safe 16) and blended at 30% weight in rated seats, 15% in unrated (safe) seats.

factors.title: Candidate quality
factors.detail: Fundamentals-only adjustments: Paxton (TX) +2.0 toward D; Brown (OH) +1.5 D; Cooper (NC) +1.5 D; Sununu (NH) 1.5 toward R. On top of the existing Collins, Osborn and Peltola terms.

factors.title: Poll cleanup
factors.detail: Generic ballot nudged D+8.4 to D+8.8 for likely voters; Democratic-sponsored polls (LA, MS) shifted 4 pts toward R at half weight; stale polls lose half their weight every 45 days after 2 weeks (VA's June poll now barely counts).

factors.title: Incumbency reweight
factors.detail: House incumbency edge cut from 3.0 to 1.8 pts; appointed senators (Husted, Moody, Graham) treated as open seats (was 1.5).

factors.title: Fat tails
factors.detail: National and race errors drawn from Student-t distributions (df 6 and 8) with the same sd, so blowouts are more likely than under a normal curve.

factors.title: Election mechanics
factors.detail: Ranked-choice transfer uncertainty in Alaska (+2.0 sd) and Maine (+1.5 sd); Montana three-way split (runner-up gets 75% of the anti-R vote); Louisiana Dec 12 House runoffs noted; independents caucus D 60% of the time.
